newsitem.title: USA: Alberta Energy plans California storage.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Energy plans California storage.

text.p: Wild Goose Storage Inc said Tuesday it filed an application with the California Public Utilities Commission for certification a proposed natural gas storage project in the southwestern corner of Butte County near the community of Gridley.
The Alberta Energy Co subsidiary said the project was acquired for undisclosed terms from Wild Goose Gas Storage LP, a Texas-based partnership of natural gas storage companies and private investors.
Wild Goose said it is seeking regulatory authorization to charge market-based rates.
Spokesman Mark Roberge declined to discuss the project's cost. The company said commercial operation of the facility is anticipated by late 1998.

In a separate statement, Alberta Energy said initial development is expected to provide working natual gas capacity of 14 billion cubic feet with firm injection capacity of 80 million cubic feet daily and withdrawla cpacity of 200 million cubic feet daily.
It said storage capacities could be expanded incrementally to meet growning market requirements and better use the high deliverability capabilities of the reservoir.
The storage project will use the depleted Wild Goose natural gas reservoir, which produced more than 100 billion cubic feet of natural gas from 1951 to the mid-1980s.
The storage site will be interconnected with Pacific Gas and Electric Co natural gas transmission and distribution system, which in turn is connected to a number of major interstate pipelines.
Currently there are ten natural gas storage facilities operating in California, most of which are owned by utilities, Wild Goose said.
